key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves multiscale CFD next-step field reconstruction by combining spectral encoding, PDE-aware attention, and self-supervised pretraining.
engineering_relevance: The approach can speed up real-world flow simulation workflows by delivering more accurate surrogate predictions of localized wake dynamics at lower computational cost.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow features
Physics-biased self-attention guided by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Across cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best aggregate accuracy, including NMSE 0.05875 and PCC 0.97019 on cylinder wake and NMSE 2.70×10^-4 on FSI.
watch_item: Performance is reported on two benchmark cases under a shared local protocol, so broader generalization to other flow regimes and longer rollout horizons still needs validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
